title: unified-rollouts-add-autorollback-workflow-for-canary-ab-shadow
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: As part of the unified rollouts initiative we need a robust automated rollback workflow that supports canary, A/B, and shadow traffic modes. Motivation: customers running Dedicated and Private deployments reported incidents where slow regressions in latency or quality went unnoticed during rolling canaries; automating safe rollbacks reduces blast radius and operational toil. This PR implements a policy-driven autorollback engine that integrates with the existing rollout controller, telemetry, and quarantine stage workflows. Key capabilities: 1) metric-driven thresholds with multi-metric composition (latency p99, error-rate, quality regression score); 2) probe-based staged shadowing to validate behavior before promotion; 3) automatic quarantine of suspect candidates with optional manual review gates; 4) rollback actions that are safe by default (weight drain + shadow disable + traffic rebalancing); 5) pluggable policy definitions per-environment and per-rollout; 6) exhaustive observability hooks and aggregated rollback reason logs. Changeset summary: - rollout-controller: add autorollback state machine and policy evaluation loop - rollout-api: new rollout.policy schema and validation + CRD examples - observability: emit rollout.rollback_reason, rollout.quarantine_events, rollout.policy_evaluation metrics - e2e-tests: new scenarios for canary, A/B, and shadow autorollback - docs: rollout autorollback guide and migration notes Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-4210) - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] e2e stability tests in perf-canary - [x] observability dashboards updated - [x] migration script for existing rollout configs Testing notes: unit tests + integration tests in CI; ran extended perf-canary in staging for 72 hours with synthetic regressions injected (latency and hallucination detectors). Observability: dashboards added under Rolling Deployments -> Autorollback; alerts tuned to avoid flapping on noisy metrics. Rollout plan: staged release to canary customers followed by gradual ramp to all hosted regions; Dedicated customers can opt-in via config flag. Migration: existing rollout objects without a policy default to safe-mode (manual rollback only). Backwards compatibility: non-breaking. See release_notes for admin-facing changes.

review_comments: Priya Shah: Can we make the default metric window configurable per-policy? Observed false positives in staging with 30s windows.
Maya Chen: Good catch — added window_ms to the policy schema and made per-environment overrides possible. Updated tests to cover the shorter and longer windows.
Omar Haddad: Engine looks good. Please add a safety guard to avoid rolling back based on transient OOM spikes (use median-based smoothing).
Maya Chen: Implemented median smoothing and added a unit test that simulates transient OOM spikes. See autorollback/metrics_smoothing_test.go
Luca Romano: e2e flaked once due to data delay in staging traces; recommend increasing retry/backoff in the probe runner.
Maya Chen: Increased probe runner backoff and added a flaky-tolerant assertion; re-ran perf-canary and verified stability.
Priya Shah: Approving after address comments and e2e green on staging.
release_notes: Add autorollback workflow for unified rollouts. Administrators can define policy-driven autorollbacks for canary, A/B, and shadow deployments. Default behavior is safe-mode (manual rollback) for existing rollouts; opt-in required for automatic action. Observability metrics and dashboards added.
migration_instructions: Existing rollout objects remain unchanged and default to manual rollback. To enable autorollback, add a rollout.policy block to the CRD or use the provided migration script scripts/migrate-rollout-policies.py. See docs/rollouts/autorollback.md for examples.
notes_for_ops: Monitor rollout.rollback_reason and rollout.quarantine_events dashboards during initial ramp. Recommended alert: >3 quarantine events within 15m for the same model -> page on-call. Use the 'rollback_reason' tag in traces for faster triage.
